body:
I've been tripping for two years straight and I don't know how to come down.  I've been off of LSD, X, weed for over two years, and I've even quit alcohol and cigarettes.  Even though, I'm completely clean, I still feel these sharp pains and visuals like I'm on a bad acid trip.
After cleaning up from using hard drugs, I decided to take a break from it all because I was having flashbacks everytime I got high.  I quit for a month and then the flashbacks died down.  After the flashbacks stopped reoccuring, I decided it was time to start smoking weed again.  Not long after I smoked a blunt, a flashback started coming along stronger than I have ever felt before.  I developed bad tunnel vision and my head felt like it was in a vice, and it felt like my whole body was caving in.  The room got smaller and everything closed in on me.  I thought it would go away (because flashbacks usually do go away after an hour or two) but this time it didn't.  After it had lasted three days, I decided I had to either kill myself or check into a mental institution because I was desperate for it to go away....
Then I found Xanax.  Xanax made it completely go away for 5 to 6 hours at a time.  But, after the xanax wore off, it always came back.   Alcohol also helped, but after it wore off the 'flashback' I was having would be worse than before (probably because of having a hangover).  So, I got hooked on Xanax and alcohol for a year and half which helped me cope, but it also killed my memory completely.  Eventually, I had to quit those because I decided it was time to face this thing sober.
Even though I'm clean, nothing has changed with this bad trip (or whatever it is).  I always feel this acid buzz, but I rarely see things that aren't there.  I do see tracers from time to time, though.  Also, whenever I watch TV with the lights off, I start to trip harder for some reason. It's more of an acid buzz than anything else.  But, it's constant, neverending, 24/7.  So, every day for two years I've been having this constant trip and I don't know what to do to stop it.
If anyone else goes through this then I do have some suggestions on how to make it more bearable...  Whenever I play the guitar I dont notice it anymore, so playing music helps take my mind completely off of it.  I do notice that when I exercise that 'the buzz' gets stronger.  I have to stay away from anything with caffiene in it because I've noticed that caffiene REALLY kicks it in to where it's hard to handle.   Whenever I'm in class, confined to a desk, this trip gets stronger.  Really anytime where I'm 'confined' to a small area, this buzz gets stronger.  Whenever I socialize with other people, I completely forget about having this problem.  I have noticed that the more I dwell on having this problem the stronger it gets, so I have to keep busy to ensure my mind is always occupied with distractions.
Recently, I've been studying religion, and that's probably the biggest thing that has helped me so far.  Religion keeps things in perspective, and helps me realize that I shouldn't be pessimistic about everything.  It's only times when I get stressed out or working under pressure that this 'trip' becomes unbearable.  I have had panic attacks (or maybe they were psychotic episodes) in the past, but I haven't had any major problems in about a year.  Things, for the most part, seem to be improving.  Even though I suffer through this every day, having hope that everything will be okay helps tremendously.  So, my advice to anyone who is going through a neverending 2 year long trip like I am, don't worry and try to focus on things in your life that make you happy.  Stay busy and don't stare at things too long without blinking.
To those who haven't taken LSD yet, I suggest that you don't do it because you might end up experiencing this 'HELL' that I am in.  I mean, even if you don't, why take the chance?  I would do just about anything to change the past, but I can't so I'll just cope the best way I know how now.
If anyone else goes through this, then post something for me to read.
